 Slugging Skincare Trend: Benefits and Side Effects
 Agency
 November 02, 2026
 Read in Nepali
 Kathmandu. Many trends related to skincare keep coming on social media, 'slugging' is also one such trend. This is a part of the Korean beauty routine. In this, a thick layer of Vaseline or petroleum jelly is applied to the face before sleeping at night. Although its main purpose is to maintain moisture in the skin, it is not an effective solution for everyone. Here we will provide information about what 'slugging' is and what its side effects are. It is believed that 'slugging' makes the skin soft, glowing, and hydrated when you wake up in the morning. Especially people with dry and dull skin can benefit from it. However, it is not suitable for all skin types. In some people, this method can cause acne, clogged pores, and skin irritation. Therefore, before adopting this method, it is important to know which people should stay away from this trend.
 What is 'Slugging'? 
 'Slugging' creates a protective layer on the skin by applying a thick layer of petroleum jelly. It does not let moisture escape from the skin. Doing so makes the skin look more hydrated, soft, and glowing. This method can be very beneficial in the winter season.
 These 4 types of people should not do 'Slugging': 
 1. If you have oily skin or frequently get acne on your face, you should avoid 'slugging'. A thick layer of Vaseline can trap oil, sweat, and dead skin cells within the skin. This can worsen acne problems and cause painful boils.
 2. If you use products containing retinol, tretinoin, glycolic acid, salicylic acid, or vitamin 'C' at night, you should not apply Vaseline on top of them. Doing so will increase the effect of these active ingredients and can cause problems like skin irritation, redness, and peeling.
 3. There are small white bumps on the skin, which contain accumulated keratin. These bumps are especially visible around the eyes and on the cheeks. Heavy products like Vaseline can worsen this problem in some people.
 4. If you have active acne, boils, wounds, or cold sores, which are viral infections, on your face, you should not do 'slugging'. In such a situation, bacteria or viruses can get trapped in the affected area, and there is a risk of increased infection.
 Instead of 'Slugging', adopt these alternatives: 
 Apply a light gel moisturizer containing niacinamide, hyaluronic acid, and centella asiatica.
 Use moisturizers containing ceramides, squalane, and fatty acids.
 You can also choose options like marula oil and rosehip seed oil.
